issues: Integrity is fine. The diff adds an SLSQP pre-solve for fresh starts (start is None). It maximizes n*mean(sqrt(r))^2, a smoothed form of the radius sum, under the same constraints, then passes the result to the normal sum-of-radii SLSQP. There is no file access, no pasted coordinates and no use of outside data. The repair step and the validity check are untouched.

No bug makes the result meaningless. np.maximum(v, 1e-12) inside the sqrt keeps the value and gradient finite. The extra 60-iteration SLSQP per restart costs time, but the restart loop is time-limited, so the 45 s void limit is not threatened.

Recomputed z: (2.9396 - 2.9366) / (0.0034 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) = 0.0030 / 0.00416 = 0.72. The harness reports 0.713; the small gap is probably from rounding of the displayed means. With only one candidate run and z well below any reasonable threshold, rejecting is consistent with the numbers.

Sanity flag, not a veto: the candidate's adjusted value of 2.9396 is above the best published value of about 2.9370 (the literature figure is about 2.9379). A mean of valid packings cannot beat the true optimum. Either the 'adjusted' value includes a noise or offset correction, or this run should be checked. The 1e-10 tolerance cannot explain a gap of 0.0026. A replicate would settle it and would also give the comparison more power.
